data.narrative:
Cerebras is a public-stage semiconductor company currently valued at $39.2B, having raised $6.6B+ to date. The valuation landscape for frontier chip designers includes a comp universe of 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, including Ouster, Aeva Technologies, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, and Etched. However, the narrow peer set presents a material constraint on valuation precision.

Peer-median triangulation is not applicable here. Of the 10 same-sector peers identified in Chips & Semiconductors, only 2 operate at the same stage and 1 at a similar valuation tier, falling short of the minimum 3-datapoint threshold required for robust median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given heterogeneity in semiconductor subsectors—from legacy foundries to specialized accelerator designers to quantum platforms. No alternative methods (DCF, revenue multiple, precedent transaction) were supported by the provided dataset.

Without sufficient narrowly-scoped comparable data or forward financials, this analysis cannot triangulate to a defensible valuation range around the $39.2B mark. The key uncertainty is Cerebras' position within the semiconductor stack: whether the company's valuation reflects specialized-hardware arbitrage or broader AI infrastructure positioning. A credible valuation conclusion would require either a larger peer cohort with aligned business models or disclosure of Cerebras' revenue and growth trajectory relative to public chip firms.
